title: Fish, mackerel, baked or broiled, coated

content.title: About
content.content: Mackerel is a marine fish from the Scombridae family, known for its rich flavor and high content of beneficial fats. When baked or broiled with a coating, it stays juicy while the crispy crust adds a pleasant texture contrast.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mackerel is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.
Coatings often use whole‑grain or rice breadcrumbs, making the dish more nutritious.
Mackerel can grow up to 5 kg and is one of the fastest‑growing fish species.
In many traditional cuisines mackerel is baked with lemon and herbs, while in Japan it is frequently prepared in tempura.

items.title: Rich source of omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3s help lower triglyceride levels, support vascular function, and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Mackerel provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 and B6 aid normal nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Mackerel supplies selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bones.

items.title: Low mercury content
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, mackerel generally contains less mercury, making it safe for regular consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium in coating
items.content: Prepared coatings often contain salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Like any sea fish, mackerel can contain trace contaminants (e.g., PCBs). Purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coated mackerel is easy to bake or grill until golden brown. Serve with lemon, fresh herbs, or a light yogurt sauce. It pairs well with vegetable sides, quinoa, or whole‑grain rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original packaging for up to 3 days. Frozen versions retain quality for up to 2 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration.
